newsitem.title: GERMANY: China's rapeseed crop seen unscathed by drought.
newsitem.headline: China's rapeseed crop seen unscathed by drought.

text.p: Rapeseed crops in China appear to be the least damaged by hot and dry conditions, with much of winter rapeseed harvested before the latest heat wave, the independent weekly Oil World newsletter said.
Most of the crop was already well developed when drought arrived in northern provinces in May, it said.
Oil World has put China's 1997/98 rapeseed crop at 9.30 million tonnes after 9.17 million in 1996/97.
But weather appears to be damaging other oilseeds.
Guangdong province, which accounts for nearly 10 percent of the groundnut area, has been hit by heavy rains in July.
Soil moisture was also very low in Shandong, Hebei and Shanxi.
Rainfall in the three provinces represented only 74 percent of the long-term average in April/June.
Together, they account for a third of the groundnut area and they are also significant cottonseed and soybean regions.
Oil World projects total Chinese oilseeds output in 1997/98 at 39.49 million tonnes after 30.03 million in the previous year.
